articles.title: BlackRock stays cautious on Indian equities despite cheaper valuations
articles.text: Mumbai: BlackRock Investment Institute is not yet ready to turn bullish on Indian equities in the near term despite valuations becoming more attractive, said Ben Powell, the firm's chief investment strategist for the Middle East and APAC. BlackRock is awaiting greater clarity on corporate earnings, crude oil prices, global bond yields and foreign fund flows before turning more positive on Indian equities."We are poised to turn a little bit more tactically constructive," said Abu Dhabi-based Powell in an interview over a video call. "The valuation is more interesting, but we want to see a bit more evidence," he said. BlackRock Investment Institute has allocated a higher share to Indian equities than their weight in global benchmarks. However, the firm remains more neutral in the near term as geopolitical risks, elevated energy prices and global yields could cloud the outlook.In India, he sees opportunities in energy, defence and manufacturing as countries respond to geopolitical uncertainty. India's benchmark indices have underperformed most large peers in 2026. The Sensex is down 14.16%, while the Nifty is down 13.5%.Read more: Nifty bears tighten grip as crude, geopolitical risks, FII outflows mount: 5 factors to decide D-Street’s fate next weekWhen asked when foreign investors could return to India, Powell said they were looking for greater stability and upward momentum in corporate earnings before increasing their exposure to Indian equities. "We just need to see a little bit more comfort on the earnings directly before we can see those flows over time," he said.Foreign investors have remained net sellers since July 2025. In 2026, they have sold Indian equities worth ₹4.55 lakh crore. According to BlackRock Investment Institute, between 2016 and 2025, about $5 of every $100 in assets acquired by households went into shares, investment funds and debt securities. Powell projects this to rise to $20 between 2026 and 2035.Read more: Swiggy may rebound to Rs 190, but charts do not signal a trend reversal: LKP’s Vatsal BhuvaCrude price impactHigher crude oil prices have posed a challenge for India as a major energy importer, but the economy has shown resilience, according to Powell. He believes that the growth outlook has remained good, although elevated energy costs would gradually feed into inflation across sectors.Brent crude oil prices have surged over 9% in the past month, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions and supply disruption fears in the Middle East. The global benchmark is trading near $116.72 per barrel.US Fed, Bond Yields & AIVolatility in South Korean and Taiwanese markets has raised questions about whether the AI investment boom has peaked. Powell said demand, earnings and capital expenditure in the sector remained strong, with money continuing to flow into AI infrastructure.While the AI investment boom continues to attract funding, higher capital costs will widen the gap between companies that generate strong returns and those that struggle, according to Powell.

Peak power demand falls as cooling needs ease
articles.text: New Delhi: India's peak power demand has eased to around 234 GW after remaining above 250 GW for much of the first half of October, as cooling and irrigation requirements begin to decline with the onset of cooler weather and rainfall in many parts of the country.The fall comes after an unusually strong power demand in September and October, when consumption remained elevated amid below-normal monsoon rainfall. Peak demand touched 260 GW on October 5, the highest ever recorded for the month, and remained close to summer levels until October 15. This demand had reached 250 GW on October 15, with only a few days in the first half of the month seeing levels below 240 GW.Also Read | Torrent Power says 3,000-MW Karjat pumped storage project outside Bhimashankar SanctuaryA government official had told ET earlier this month that electricity demand was expected to decline as the pressure on cooling appliances and irrigation reduced. However, states such as Gujarat and Tamil Nadu continue to see high peak demand. In Gujarat, the peak demand on October 24 was around 28.3 GW, which is almost the same as in much of June. "This could be because of the weather-related demand and some industrial demand moving to the grid," an industry official said.Also Read | Adani Power CEO puts Q2 numbers in perspective, gives a peek into the road aheadSeptember had recorded an increase of around 11% in electricity consumption. The sustained demand had also kept electricity prices elevated in the short-term market. Prices in the day-ahead market of the Indian Energy Exchange were hovering above ₹7 per unit during the first half of October. Coal stocks at domestic coal-based power plants stood at 17.3 million tonnes as of October 24, compared with 17.9 million tonnes on October 15 and 18.5 million tonnes at the b ginning of the month.

articles.title: ISRO Plans to Expand Launch Infrastructure with Four Pads by 2029
articles.text:
Isro Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by 2029.He outlined the agency’s roadmap, which includes a 2,000-acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district to meet the global demand for satellite deployment.
Clarifying that the national space agency will not be privatised, Narayanan emphasised that partnering with private firms was essential to meet surging global and domestic demands for thousands of satellites.
“To handle this expanding ecosystem, Isro will handhold startups and private enterprises, transferring technological expertise to foster economic growth and generate thousands of high-tech jobs,” he said while speaking at a graduation ceremony at a private university here on Saturday.
“India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by 2029, supported by an increasing reliance on private industry partnerships to handle commercial operations,” Narayanan said.
The Isro chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems.
Stating that Isro plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission, he said, “These tests will evaluate environmental control, safety systems, crew escape mechanisms, and module interiors under varying pressure, temperature, and humidity conditions.”
He said Isro successfully conducted approximately 8,000 ground-based experiments for the mission, and four astronaut-designates are currently undergoing specialised training.
Looking further ahead, Narayanan revealed plans for Chandrayaan-5, a collaborative lunar mission with Japan’s space agency featuring a 350-kg rover designed to conduct 100 days of surface experiments.

articles.title: Air Chief AP Singh Says Operation Sindoor Demonstrated IAF’s Reach
articles.text:
The Indian Air Force’s calibrated strikes across the Western front during Operation Sindoor — spanning 1,200 km in breadth and 200 km in depth–demonstrated that no target is beyond its reach, Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh said on Sunday, in an apparent warning to Pakistan.
In an exclusive interview with PTI, the Air Chief described the operation as a validation of the IAF’s capability-centric approach, emphasising that it reaffirmed air power’s decisive role as both the nation’s primary responder and its strategic deterrent. At the same time, the IAF Chief cautioned that validation of the IAF’s approach must not be a reason to “stand still” as the way forward is to deepen and widen this capability across the force.
“Operationally, one lesson stands out: we must always retain multiple options and the ability to adapt rapidly as the adversary changes tactics,” the Chief of Air Staff who oversaw the four-day operation said.
“A capability-centric force is inherently better at this, because it can draw on many tools rather than depend on one. That same flexibility allowed us to calibrate our response and keep control of escalation,” he said.
Launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, Operation Sindoor saw India carry out precision strikes against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied territories in May last year– marking the most daring cross-border military action by the country since the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War.
“Operation Sindoor proved that the path we have chosen is the right one. We will continue along it with even greater resolve, so that if the nation calls upon us again, the IAF responds more swiftly, more precisely and more decisively, on the nation’s terms,” he said.
The Chief of the Air Staff also noted that some of the indigenously developed weapons systems performed “exceptionally”, delivering crippling blows deep into enemy territory, and that the IAF honoured its commitment to “zero collateral damage” throughout the operation.
“Operation Sindoor was, above all, a validation of the capability-centric approach the IAF has been pursuing. We have moved from thinking in terms of individual platforms to thinking in terms of capability, where every aircraft, sensor, weapon and network is integrated so that the combined effect is far greater than the sum of the parts,” the IAF Chief said.
“The operation put that philosophy to the test in real operations, and it delivered. It reaffirmed the decisive role of air power as both the nation’s primary responder and its strategic deterrent, and it reinforced the enduring importance of speed, precision, integration and adaptability,” he said.
The Air Chief Marshal was responding to a question on the IAF’s key takeaways from Operation Sindoor across operational tactics, strategic options, setbacks, and firepower.
The operation’s success did not come from any single weapon or platform. It came from the combined effect of accurate intelligence, networked operations, stand-off and precision weapons, electronic warfare, layered air defence and counter-UAS (Unmanned Aerial Systems) capabilities, all working as one system, he said.
“On the offensive side, calibrated targeting across the entire front, spanning 1,200 km in breadth and 200 km in depth, made it clear that no place is beyond the IAF’s reach,” he said.
“Some of our indigenously developed weapons performed exceptionally, delivering crippling blows deep into enemy territory, and we honoured our commitment to zero collateral damage throughout,” he said.
The Chief of the Air Staff said India’s home-grown networked air defence defeated the large number of drones and stand-off weapons launched by the Pakistan military as the nation could act with confidence.
“Offence and defence reinforced each other, which is precisely what a capability-centric force is designed to achieve,” he said.
Air Chief Marshal Singh said Operation Sindoor also demonstrated the value of joint and multi-domain integration, adding bringing together the air, land, maritime, space, cyber and electromagnetic domains enabled faster decision-making and greater operational effect.
The IAF Chief, however, said the force must now focus on strengthening combat mass, ISR (intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) prowess, electronic warfare, counter-UAS capability, resilient networks and AI-enabled decision support.
“Equally, we must build the ability to sustain high-intensity operations over time through robust logistics, maintenance, infrastructure and, above all, indigenous production. Work is already under way on each of these fronts.
Air Chief Marshal Singh said the IAF’s vision is closely aligned with the larger national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, as a developed India must also be a secure and resilient India.
“The Defence Forces Vision 2047 likewise envisages an integrated, multi-domain and technologically advanced military in support of this national ambition,” he said.
For the IAF, the Chief of Air Staff said it means evolving into a multi-domain aerospace force capable of protecting India’s growing economic, technological and strategic interests across the entire spectrum of conflict.
“We have set out a clear, structured path towards that goal. The IAF’s Capability Perspective Plan-2047 lays down long-term priorities based on emerging technologies, and it feeds into ten-year plans that are updated periodically,” he said.
In the space domain, the Air Chief Marshal said the broader direction is reflected in the IAF Space Vision 2047.
“Our emphasis will be on ‘Aatmanirbharta’, advanced aerospace technologies, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, space, cyber, precision weapons and resilient networks. Just as important, we will build the industrial ecosystem needed to sustain all of these capabilities,” he said.
The IAF Chief argued that a secure India creates the environment for economic growth, while a technologically and economically stronger India provides the foundation for greater strategic power.
“Realising this vision will require a whole-of-nation approach, and the IAF is committed to playing its full part,” he said.
“By 2047, we aim to be one of the world’s most capable, innovative and technologically self-reliant aerospace forces, a force that stands as both the guardian and a driver of a developed India,” he noted.

articles.title: Indian Army Selects Hild’s Talon K for AI Interceptor UAV
articles.text:
The Indian Army has selected Chennai-based Hild Defence and Aerospace to develop an AI-enabled high-speed interceptor UAV for counter-drone operations, another move towards using unmanned aircraft as part of the counter-UAS layer.
The development requirement was floated on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for the Army’s establishment in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. The tender sought one development system rather than an immediate fleet purchase. GeM-linked records show that Hild emerged as the lowest bidder and the tender was awarded on 18 September 2026. Hild offered its Talon K against the Army requirement and emerged as L1 at approximately ₹10.13 lakh.
Shri Krishna Traders was L2 at about ₹10.18 lakh, while Future Vision Enterprises was L3 at approximately ₹14.88 lakh. The tender’s published estimated value was ₹44.36 lakh. The tender attracted 11 bids, but only three bidders were ultimately listed as technically qualified: Hild Defence and Aerospace, Future Vision Enterprises and Shri Krishna Traders. Eight other bidders were listed as disqualified, including InsideFPV Ventures, Vetaal Defence, Tactix Defence Systems, Skayfarm Solutions, Urban Dienst, Dhawan Enterprises, Gokal Ram Govt Contractor and individual bidder Praduman Thakur. The requirement is significant because it seeks an interceptor UAV, rather than another conventional surveillance or strike drone.
The Army has been expanding its counter-drone capabilities across detection, electronic warfare and kinetic systems. An interceptor UAV introduces another approach, in which an unmanned aircraft can be used to engage an incoming hostile drone. In May Janes reported that the company had received Indian Army orders for its Atlas mortar-dropping quadcopter and approximately 30 Talon FPV UAVs.
Hild said the Talon has an operational range of 10-20 km depending on configuration and can carry up to a 3 kg payload. The Army’s decision to fund development rather than immediately procure a large fleet also allows the service to evaluate whether the proposed interceptor can meet operational requirements before wider induction. The project could eventually add an airborne kinetic layer to existing counter-UAS systems, particularly where electronic jamming alone may not be sufficient against drones operated to operate through contested electromagnetic environments.
Edited By Raunak Kunde

articles.title: HAL Seeks 10 Indigenous Maritime Patrol Radar Sets for DO-228
articles.text:
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has further extended the deadline for bids to supply 10 indigenous maritime patrol radar sets in a tender from its Transport Aircraft Division in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. According to the latest reported extension, the closing date for submissions will now be 30 October 2026.
Listed on the GeM portal as bid GEM/2026/B/7783335, the tender is for 10 radar sets specified under the Aerospace and Defence category. According to the tender summary, the procuring organisation is HAL’s Transport Aircraft Division, Kanpur. The proposal is based on a total value, and the bidders need to submit documents on relevant experience, turnover and a certificate as stipulated in the additional terms and conditions.
The procurement deadline has repeatedly been extended: it was initially opened on 14 July 2026, and the deadline was extended to 17 August, then to 7 September, to 5 October and to 15 October in a corrigendum. There is a further report that another amendment was published on 18 October, setting the new closing date at 30 October.
The document states that the earnest money deposit (EMD) will be mentioned in the bid document and that exemption from EMD payment is ineffective. No mention was made there of a tender fee.
The procurement appears to be part of a broader project of integrating an indigenous maritime patrol radar in HAL’s Dornier 228. In July 2024, HAL’s Transport Aircraft Division published an earlier request for proposal, specifying Tender No. DO-228/MPR/1 for the integration of an airworthy-certified indigenous maritime patrol radar with its line-replaceable equipment (LRUs) on to the Dornier 228 aircraft. That procurement included activities related to the process of integration and conducting ground and flight trials as well as carrying out certifications by the Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification (CEMILAC) and the Directorate General of Aeronautical Quality Assurance (DGAQA).
It appears that the proposed procurement of 10 radar sets could be another initiative in the same project, possibly specifying the next tranche of 10 sets, as the first procurement specified 19 radar sets. However, the documents provided do not refer to any connection between the procurement.
An indigenous maritime patrol radar could provide surveillance coverage for coastal waters and approaches to a ship according to its design, performance characteristics and the capabilities as well its host aircraft’s equipment. Such a radar could be useful for providing domain awareness. If the aircraft is equipped with this kind of radar, the crew can detect some surface vessels at sea within its operational range, and the specifics of this system’s performance will determine what types of targets and at what distances it can detect. But the precise performance of the radar sought by HAL cannot be established according to the available documentation.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE
